# Build a multi-window dashboard with Dock Layouts: the implementation post

## Context

Stage 2 of the operator's two-stage blog post (2026-10-11), and the second entry in the series order recorded on #13383 ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/13383#issuecomment-6110673720)). Stage 1, `learn/blog/multi-window-dashboards-with-dock-layouts.md` (#19602, merged as `97112ed5ea`), shows what the person at the dashboard gets. It ends on two configs and a promise: "The next post in this series builds a workspace end to end."

## The Problem

- **Angle:** build one dashboard workspace from an empty app to panes that leave the window and come home. Each step is a decision the developer owns, shown with code that runs.
- **Audience:** developers who read stage 1 and want to try it. Neo knowledge is optional, and each step links its guide.
- **Sources to mine (nothing invented):**
  - `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsAdoption.md` (the five decisions; its default tear-out contract as corrected by #19608);
  - `DockLayoutsWindows.md`, `DockLayoutsStateAndPersistence.md`, `DockLayoutsPanes.md` and `DockLayoutsStyling.md`;
  - `learn/tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout.md`;
  - `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` (`enableDockTearOutLifecycle`, `openTearOutVessel`, `canOpenTearOutVessel`, `perspectives`, the action flags);
  - the Workstation (`apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs`, its `BootIntent`, its IndexedDB persistence);
  - `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/Viewport.mjs` (the empty boot page);
  - `examples/dashboard/dock/MainContainer.mjs` (perspectives, saved layouts).

## The Architectural Reality

Docs only: `learn/blog/<slug>.md`, a `blog.json` leaf, and images in `neomjs/pages` under `resources_pub/website/blog/<slug>/`. A code block is shown in the post only after it has run, live in the Portal or in an app the post names.

## The Fix

One post, ordered the way a developer would build:
1. panes and zones;
2. pane policies (lock, pin, close);
3. named perspectives and saving a layout;
4. turning on windows (`useSharedWorkers`, the tear-out opt-in, the cross-window sort group, the empty page a torn-out window boots into);
5. styling with tokens;
6. the keyboard path.

The bounds come from the guides, not memory.

**Plan (2026-10-11, from a read of the corrected Adoption guide):**
- **Live where the Portal can run it.** Blog posts render `javascript live-preview` blocks (the v10 deep dives use them). Steps 1–3 and the action flags run as live, editable previews: panes and zones, per-pane policy (`closable`/`movable`/`pinnable` on the declaration), and `perspectives` + `activePerspective` behind a toolbar (the dock example's `dockShellIndex` pattern).
- **Read-only where it cannot.** A torn-out window reopens the host document with `?tearout=<itemId>`, which a live preview inside the Portal cannot answer. The windows step is read-only code checked against `Workspace.mjs`, and the reader runs it in the Workstation. Persistence (`Persistence.createSavedLayout` / `restoreSavedLayout`) and styling tokens (`.neo-dock-workspace .neo-dashboard`) are read-only too.
- Every live block is render-verified in the Portal before review, and every read-only block's symbols are checked at the PR's base.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every code block runs, either in the Portal's live preview or in an app the post names, and the PR records where each one ran. (#19618, merged as `ca3b95460f`; steps 1–3 run headless in the Portal, steps 4–6 match the examples they name)
- [x] The windows section matches `Workspace.mjs` and the corrected Adoption guide at the PR's base: what the engine owns, and what the application supplies. (at the PR's base; the addon list gets a re-read against #19622, see the follow-up ticket)
- [x] It links stage 1 for the benefits and does not repeat them.
- [x] Registered in `blog.json` and render-verified on the Portal.
- [x] At least two model reviews, one from a non-Claude family; the operator approves last. (Euclid, GPT: APPROVED round 2; the operator merged)
- [x] No client names.

## Out of Scope

Engine changes, and the benefits story (stage 1).

* docs(blog): from two configs to a second screen, building a dashboard with Dock Layouts (#19614)

Stage 2 of the Dock Layouts series: six build steps. Steps 1-3 are live previews (panes and zones; closable/pinnable policy on edge panes; perspectives behind a toolbar bound to dock.perspective), each run headless in the Portal: the policy pane lacks close and unpin while its neighbour has both; Incident rearranges, a move shows Modified, Monitor restores. Steps 4-6 are read-only code matching the examples they name (the dock example's save/restore, examples/dashboard/tearOut from #19617, the Adoption guide's tokens). movable:false is described as implemented (it refuses cross-document transfers only), not as the guides imply; a defect-note records the mismatch.

* docs(blog): step 5 shows the main-thread addons a multi-window dock needs (#19614)

The defaults are DragDrop, Navigator and Stylesheet. Without WindowPosition a window dragged by its title bar paints no drop zones over another (Grace's 18:43Z finding on the FM cockpit), so the post now shows the example's full list and says what WindowPosition and DockFlip do.

* docs(blog): step 5 describes the tear-out witness as a typed draft (#19614)

Follows #19617's RA-1 fix: a pane id survives a re-create, so the example's e2e test checks a draft typed into the Notes pane, and the post now says so.

* docs(blog): step 4 shows the read-back restore, and the footer names the Brain as the Agent OS (#19614)
